>
> ## Relevant official text
>
> Wholesale gas on Australia's east coast is expected to be well supplied in quarter 4 of 2026, but further investment is needed to meet long-term demand.
>
> The east coast gas market is predicted to have a surplus of 13 petajoules (PJ) in quarter 4 of 2026 if LNG producers export all their uncontracted gas. This is the highest forecast quarter 4 surplus since 2023. The east coast is also forecast to be well supplied in quarters 1 and 4 of 2027.
>
> Supply over winter 2027 is expected to be tight. There is a risk of shortfalls in quarters 2 and 3 of 2027 if LNG producers export all their uncontracted gas. Higher production volumes in coming quarters could be used to fill storage facilities ahead of increased demand next winter.
>
> Global energy price disruptions had not materially affected domestic gas prices at the time of the report. Spot prices were below 2025 averages. Prices under contracts agreed in the first quarter of 2026 for supply in 2027 were lower than in the previous quarter and broadly in line with pre-conflict levels.
>
> Queensland LNG producers and their associates control 84 per cent of commercially viable gas resources. The ACCC identified Victoria's Iona Underground Gas Storage facility as critical to southern state markets, while commercial and technical constraints may limit the availability of unused capacity at other storage facilities.
>
> The ACCC scheduled its next interim Gas Inquiry report for September 2026.
